_doc: Short-prompt, short-output jobs meant for the helper sub-agent (CPU-friendly). Gold labels are deliberately unambiguous.

classify.text: A bear wandered into camp at night and mauled a sleeping hunter.
Two neighbours shared a pot of stew and laughed about old times.
Ayo noticed that clay hardens when left in the fire overnight.
Old Teku died in his sleep after a long illness.
The shaman saw a white stag in a dream and says it is a sign from the ancestors.
Two clans fought with spears over the hunting grounds by the lake.
A traveller exchanged three flint blades for a bundle of furs.
Mira gave birth to healthy twins at dawn.
A rockslide blocked the only path down the mountain.
The children made up a new game with pebbles and taught it to everyone.
Someone stole the chief's ceremonial necklace and a fight broke out over who did it.
The family's only goat was carried off by a flood.

names.feature: a fishing village at a river mouth
a flint quarry in the hills
a grove where the dead are buried

summarize.dialogue:
Brann: You took more than your share of the catch again.
Ama: I have three children to feed!
Brann: So do I. Don't expect my help when your roof leaks.

Cyra: Your leg is bleeding, sit down.
Doru: It's nothing.
Cyra: Let me wrap it with moss. There. Lean on me on the way back.
Doru: Thank you, I owe you.

Esk: I saw you whispering to the elders about me.
Fen: I only said you were tired lately.
Esk: Liar. You told them I was lazy.

Galo: I found a spot where the berries grow thick. Come, I'll show you.
Hesa: You'd share it? Nobody shares berry spots.
Galo: You helped me last winter. Fair is fair.

Ira: Will you hold the rope while I climb?
Juno: Sure.
(Juno let go of the rope halfway and walked off laughing.)
Ira: I could have died!

memories: A wolf bit my cousin near the berry bushes last winter.
The elders laughed at my fish trap at the evening fire.
Cyra wrapped my wounded leg with moss and helped me home.
Lightning burned the granary and half our winter food.
I nearly drowned crossing the river last summer.
A traveller traded me flint blades for furs.
My mother taught me to find honey by following bees.
The headwoman made a rule about burying food for the earth mother.

queries.q: Is the river safe to cross?
Who has been kind to me?
Are there dangerous animals near food?
What happened to the village food stores?
How do people react to my inventions?
Where can I get good stone tools?
